specific_rules: Angles and plates for structural steel framing to conform to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted
Channels for structural steel framing to conform to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted
Steel W shapes (I sections) and tees to conform to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted
Hollow structural sections for framing to conform to NBN EN 10210 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted

Structural steel to conform to requirements listed on Structural General Notes; subcontractor to adopt subgrade selection per NBN EN 1993-1-10 and Belgian National Annex for fittings and designed items
Steel sections for metal fabrications to comply with EN 10025
Steel hollow sections for metal fabrications to comply with EN 10210
Plates for metal fabrications to comply with ISO 3574 and ISO 6317
Steel sections for stairs and guards to comply with EN 10025

materials.category: Cold-Formed / Coated Steel for Decking and Sheet Items
materials.grade_or_type: S350 galvanized sheet and commercial quality sheets
specific_rules: Deck units and sheet accessories to be produced from galvanized steel sheet conforming to NBN EN 10346 and NBN EN 10143, Grade of Steel S350 unless indicated or agreed otherwise
Deck units must be free of dirt, rust, rolling oils or other materials detrimental to bond of field-applied finishes
Roof deck to be wide rib units with no stiffening ribs in the top surface
Ungalvanized steel sheet for stairs and guards to be hot- or cold-rolled; use cold-rolled where finished work is exposed to view
Hot-rolled steel sheet to comply with ISO 4995 (commercial steel)
Cold-rolled steel sheet to comply with ISO 4997 (commercial steel)
Steel tubing for stairs and guards to be structural tubing per ISO 10799, round and shapes as indicated
Pipe materials to comply with ISO 4200 for plain end welded or seamless steel tubes
Cold reduced steel sheet of commercial and drawing qualities to comply with ISO 3574 for certain plate items
Bolts, nuts and washers for structural steel framing to comply with NBN EN 1090, Grade 8.8 unless noted otherwise
Anchor bolts for structural steel framing to comply with NBN EN 15048 with grade as specified in design documents; non-headed type unless otherwise indicated
High strength bolts for structural steel accessories to conform to NBN EN 1993 and NBN EN 14399
All bolts used in structural steel framing to be new and not re-used
Direct tension indicators for structural steel to meet requirements of NBN EN 14399
Washers in structural steel to conform to NBN EN 1993
Washers in contact with high-strength bolt heads and nuts to conform to NBN EN 14399
Bevelled washers to be square, smooth and sloped so that contact surfaces of bolt head and nut are parallel
Bolts, nuts and washers for metal fabrications to comply with EN ISO 898; provide zinc coated fasteners for exterior use or where built into exterior walls
Fasteners for metal fabrications to be selected for required type, grade and class and to be zinc coated where exposed or embedded
Mechanical fasteners for steel deck to be proprietary systems (e.g., Hilti or approved alternative) with capacity proven by diaphragm calculations
Sidelap connectors for steel deck to be proprietary mechanical systems (Hilti or approved alternative)
Anchorage devices for handrails and railings to include drilled-in expansion anchors and self-tapping screws of adequate size and type to support structural loads

materials.grade_or_type: Proprietary headed studs per EN ISO 13918 / BS EN ISO 13918
specific_rules: Shear stud connectors in structural steel framing to be proprietary type with minimum yield strength of 350 N/mm2 and minimum ultimate tensile strength of 450 N/mm2 and minimum elongation of 15 percent to BS EN ISO 13918

Stud shear connectors for steel decking to be proprietary type with minimum yield strength of 350 N/mm2 and minimum ultimate tensile strength of 450 N/mm2 and minimum elongation of 15 percent to EN ISO 13918
Stud shear connectors to be shop welded using automatic end welding of headed studs in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions for composite construction
Top surface of beams receiving welded studs to be free from mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint or other substances detrimental to welding and cleaned prior to laying decking
Stud welding not permitted when ambient temperature is below 0 degrees C
Weld studs through steel deck into primary steel members below for composite action

materials.grade_or_type: Per EN 1011, EN 1090 and NBN EN ISO 9606-1 / 14732
specific_rules: Welding materials for structural steel to comply with NBN EN 1090 and other listed codes for welding consumables, appropriate for materials being welded
Welding electrodes for structural steel to conform to relevant standards listed in reference standards, specifically Group 5 of NBN EN 1993-1-8
Welding materials for metal fabrications to comply with EN 1011 requirements
Qualify welding processes and welding operators for metal fabrications in accordance with EN 1011
Welders employed on structural steel works to be qualified in line with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 within the previous 12 months
Welders for steel decking shear stud welding to be certified by recognized authority in project location and qualified per relevant welding standards
Welding for stairs, ramps, handrails and guards to comply with EN 1011 and EN ISO 2553 for symbolic representation on drawings and EN 1011-3 for stainless steel where applicable
Grout for structural steel column base plates to be non-shrink, non-metallic aggregate type capable of developing a minimum compressive strength of 35 MPa at 28 days
Grout for structural steel interfaces to comply with Structural General Notes and manufacturer’s instructions for non-shrink grout
Grout to be used solidly between column plates and bearing surfaces and trowelled smooth, splaying neatly to 45 degrees
Shrink-resistant grout to be submitted as part of structural steel submittals

materials.category: Primers and Paints for Structural Steel
materials.grade_or_type: Rust inhibitive shop primer, inorganic zinc-rich primer, alkyd primers
specific_rules: Shop and touch-up primer for structural steel to be fabricator’s standard grey rust-inhibitive primer, complying with VOC limitations of authorities having jurisdiction
Touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces to be fabricator’s standard, complying with VOC limitations
Primary steelwork to be protected with paint systems conforming to NBN EN ISO 12944 unless noted otherwise
Members exposed to exterior outside controlled building environment to receive inorganic zinc-rich primer with minimum 60% volume solids and at least 85% metallic zinc in dry film
Where steel surfaces receive sprayed-on or intumescent paint fireproofing, shop primer must be a heavy duty alkyd compatible with the intumescent system

Shop coat to be applied within four hours after blast cleaning and before rust bloom occurs; apply only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point
Coating thickness of each coat to be checked during application using wheel or comb gauge in accordance with NBN EN ISO 2808

Finish must not slump, flow, crack, flake, split, sag, pit, bubble, blister, float, effloresce, craze, shrink, break, wrinkle, crinkle, yellow, chalk, fade, discolor, powder, stain, bleed or lose finish or gloss within specified service life
All finishes to be uniform in texture, colour and appearance within control sample limits and free from irregularities or distortion
Intumescent coatings to be factory-mixed formulations consisting of single-pack thin-film materials suitable for spray application

System 1 for internal steelwork (C1, off-site application): Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent coating, DFT to achieve required fire resistance, with Sherwin Williams FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer at nominal 25 microns DFT as defined by EN ISO 12944-5 and FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer at nominal 50 microns DFT

Under certain circumstances FIRETEX FX2003 may be applied directly to steel blast cleaned to minimum Sa 2.5 (EN ISO 8501-1) with surface profile 50-100 microns; to be confirmed with manufacturer’s technical department

System 2 for internal steelwork (C1, off-site application): Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002 ultra-fast drying intumescent coating, DFT to achieve required fire resistance, used with FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer (25 microns nominal DFT) and FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer (50 microns nominal DFT) as per EN ISO 12944-5
Designer of record to adjust total DFT makeup of primer, intumescent basecoat and top sealer for alternate environmental corrosivity classifications (C2, C3, C4, etc.)
All intumescent systems to be tested in accordance with EN 13381-4 and classified to EN 13501 with assessments issued by organizations following the Passive Fire Protection Federation guidance
Intumescent coating systems must be compatible with underlying primers and other surface coatings; compatibility to be certified by manufacturer

materials.grade_or_type: Carbon steel and stainless steel grades
specific_rules: Standard structural steel sections for metal fabrications to comply with EN 10025
Steel hollow sections for fabrications to comply with EN 10210
Pipe for barrier rails and miscellaneous items to comply with ISO 4200
Stainless steel for specific items to comply with EN 10088, Grade 1.4436 where specified for stairs
Gratings for fabrications to comply with NAAMM MBG 531 or NAAMM MBG 532 based on bar sizes

Ladders in metal fabrications to be steel with galvanized finish, with manufacturer’s standard steel flat bar side rails, rectangular steel rungs 20–50 mm and spacing as specified; galvanized after fabrication
Barrier rails to use 40 mm diameter steel pipe and steel channel sections with galvanized finish
Ledge angles, shelf angles, channels and plates not attached to structural framing for support of metal decking to be galvanized
Concrete edge confinement angles to be steel angles with galvanized finish designed to receive integral anchor bolts (anchorage welded full perimeter fillet 2.5 mm, spacing as shown)
Downspout guards and cantilevered canopy supports to be galvanized steel fabrications
Roof opening framing to be steel with either prime paint or galvanized finish
Metal bent plates at conductor heads and steel corner guards to be fabricated per details with appropriate finishes

materials.category: Metal Stairs, Ramps, Handrails and Guards
materials.grade_or_type: Carbon steel, galvanized steel, aluminum tread plates, bar gratings
specific_rules: Metal stairs to include landing platforms, vertical and horizontal supports, railings and guards; fabricated for anchorage to building structure
Stair assemblies and railings to be designed to meet local code requirements and specified live loads and deflection limits

Stairs with concrete treads to use metal pans of minimum 2 mm thickness and 50 mm depth welded to carrier angles on stringers; risers closed; pans later filled with concrete (concrete detailing out of scope)

Alternative stair treads to be galvanized mild steel or aluminium checker plate (e.g. Durbar or similar) with minimum 3 mm thickness; welded to carrier angles on stringers with support profiles below treads as required by structural calculations

Risers for these stairs to be same material and thickness as tread pans with sloped riser and rounded nosing; nosing overhang not more than 25 mm and nosing return flush with top of finished tread and not more than 12.5 mm wide
Stringers to be rolled steel channels with nominal depth of 300 mm for both stairs and ramps
End closures of stringers to be sheet steel of same thickness as risers welded across ends
Landings to be of same construction as treads, supported and reinforced to achieve design load capacity
Public access stair railings to be steel tubular pipe railings with smooth continuous handrail and welded seams or concealed couplings
Access-only stair railings to use steel tubular pipe with tube clamp system (Kee Clamp or similar approved)

Railings for stairs and ramps with open grating to use steel bar grating treads and ramps with open grid and minimum openings per local code; bearing bars minimum 37.5 mm depth; nosings non-slip and contrasting colour with minimum 30 mm width
Railings for stairs and ramps with open grating to be galvanized after fabrication or coated per local corrosion level; see also steel coatings section 09 97 13
Stairs and landings at electrical platforms to have bolted connections allowing removal and replacement for equipment maintenance
Stepovers (bridge-style roof stairs) to be bigfoot-mounted and designed for height and wind loads to comply with EN 14122

Fixed ladders in stairs section to use manufacturer’s standard steel tubes, plates, bars, shapes, sheets, wire and mesh per materials article; rails to be steel flats; rungs 20–50 mm rectangular steel maximum 600 mm wide; vertical spacing 225–300 mm; maximum 6 m height between landings
Fixed ladder guardrails to be 1100 mm high to EN 14122; landings with open grid or expanded metal with self-closing trap doors; safety cage hoops formed from circular flat steel plate above 3 m
Handrails to be round pipe rails of nominal 32 mm diameter unless otherwise indicated
Guard top rails to be continuous round pipe or tube of nominal 50 mm diameter, sloped parallel to stair pitch with heights per local code and minimum 1100 mm on landings
Infill for picket railings to be vertical solid steel square bars 12.5 mm square at maximum 100 mm centres, welded to top and bottom rails
Infill for pipe railings to be pipe or tube rails of 50 mm nominal diameter sloped parallel to stair pitch with height per local code
End and intermediate posts for guards to be same material and size as top rails with maximum spacing 1.5 m and mounted by welding to top of stringer

Handrail and railing members to be interconnected by butt welding or internal connectors; tee and cross intersections formed by mitred ends and all-around welds or prefabricated fittings; curves formed by bending in jigs to maintain circular cross section
Handrails to have wall returns at ends of wall-mounted segments and extend beyond first/last nosing line as required by local code
Exposed pipe rail ends to be closed by welding 2 mm thick plates or using prefabricated fittings; drain and vent holes located inconspicuously and plugged before delivery
Guardrails for fixed ladders and platforms to meet EN 14122 requirements including 1100 mm height and appropriate configuration
All external handrail, stair and ramp components to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for a C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2 and ISO 9223

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Blast Cleaning and Surface Preparation for Steel
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: ISO 8501-1, EN ISO 8503-1, EN ISO 8503-2, EN ISO 8502-3
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Structural steel surfaces to be blast cleaned to Sa 2.5 (ISO 8501-1) starting from initial rust grade A or B. Use suitable abrasives free from fines, water and oil and remove abrasive residues. Remove all surface defects detrimental to the protective paint system. Blast clean only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point. Remove all traces of blast residue and dust and prevent contamination of surfaces; require workers to wear clean gloves when handling blast cleaned steel. Surface roughness and profile to meet EN ISO 8503-1 and EN ISO 8503-2 requirements. Dust and contamination to be controlled and checked visually or as per EN ISO 8502-3 for intumescent fireproofing preparation.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Corrosion Protection – General Painting for Structural Steel
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: NBN EN ISO 12944, NBN EN ISO 12944-1, NBN EN ISO 12944-2, NBN EN ISO 12944-5, EN ISO 17463
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply corrosion protection systems to all primary steelwork to NBN EN ISO 12944 unless noted otherwise. Corrosivity classifications per NBN EN ISO 12944-2: internal steelwork C2 and external steelwork C4 unless overridden by project documentation. Ensure compatibility between corrosion protection system and intumescent paint system and comply with Section 07 81 23. Submit proposals including durability ranges per NBN EN ISO 12944-1; standard ranges from low (L, up to 7 years) to very high (VH, over 25 years). Use coating products according to manufacturers’ instructions and verify they are recommended for the specific surface and exposure conditions and compatible with each other. During application, check coat thickness with wheel or comb gauges as per EN ISO 2808. All finishes must be uniform and free of defects such as slumping, cracking, blistering, chalking or discoloration and must meet agreed sample appearance. Conduct anticorrosive performance assessment of organic coatings in accordance with EN ISO 17463 where specified.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: Fabricator’s rust inhibitive primer, NBN EN ISO 2808
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply specified shop primer coat within four hours after blast cleaning and before any rust bloom occurs, with application restricted to relative humidity below 85% and steel temperature at least 3 °C above dew point. Use fabricator’s standard grey rust-inhibitive primer complying with VOC regulations. Measure dry film thickness of each coat during application using gauges in accordance with NBN EN ISO 2808. Ensure final coated surfaces remain free from slumping, flowing, cracking, flaking, splitting, sagging, pitting, bubbling, blistering, crazing, shrinking, wrinkling, chalking, fading, discoloration, powdering or staining during specified service life. Paint all structural steel except members encased in concrete, exterior members outside controlled building environments (which require inorganic zinc-rich primer with at least 60% volume solids and minimum 85% metallic zinc in film), contact surfaces of welded connections and areas within 50 mm of field welds, contact surfaces of slip-critical high-strength bolted connections, surfaces receiving sprayed-on or intumescent fireproofing (which require a compatible heavy duty alkyd primer), and surfaces receiving field-welded studs. Perform touch-up painting after erection on welds, abrasions and unprimed areas using identical primer to same standard as shop coat.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Galvanizing – Structural Steel and Metal Fabrications
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: For components to be galvanized, complete all cutting, welding and drilling before galvanizing. Provide all necessary vent and drain holes in approved locations designed per EN ISO 14713-1 guidance to prevent air pockets and ensure complete zinc coverage; seal vent and drain holes to approval after galvanizing. Design large articles to minimize risk of distortion during hot-dip galvanizing; consider single-dip galvanizing for large elements and splicing structures if single dip is not possible. Prefer hot rolled sections over cold formed sections where possible to reduce internal stresses and distortion risk. Avoid excessive jigs before welding, minimize weld amount and size to reduce heat input, and use balanced welding procedures and uniform steel thickness where practical. Galvanize structural steel members after fabrication to EN ISO 1461. Galvanize ladders, barrier rails, ledge and shelf angles, concrete edge confinement angles, downpipe guards, cantilevered canopy supports, and roof opening framing as indicated. For external and exposed metal fabrications including handrails and associated components, provide factory pre-finished coatings suitable for C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2 and ISO 9223.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Shop Priming and Galvanizing for Metal Fabrications
finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C4 for external/exposed, NOT SPECIFIED for internal
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN ISO 8503-1, EN ISO 1461, EN ISO 12944-2, ISO 9223, EN ISO 17463
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Prime paint all steel items except where otherwise indicated. Galvanize items embedded in concrete or masonry. Do not prime surfaces in direct contact with concrete, where site welding is required, or on items to receive sprayed fireproofing. Clean surfaces of rust, scale, grease and foreign matter before finishing, with surface preparation compatible with coating manufacturer’s requirements and EN ISO 8503-1 for roughness. Apply one coat of grey metal primer or approved equal to a minimum dry film thickness of 50 microns. Hot-dip galvanize structural steel members and other designated items to EN ISO 1461 requirements. Touch up abraded galvanized areas after fabrication using specified touch-up primer meeting EN ISO 17463 anticorrosion performance guidelines. All external and exposed metal fabrications and associated components to be pre-finished in factory to a system suitable for C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C1 for defined systems, adaptable to C2–C4
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN 16623, EN 13381-4, EN 13501, EN ISO 12944-5, ASFP Yellow Book, ASFP TGD 11, EN ISO 8501-1, EN ISO 8503-2, EN ISO 8502-3
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply intumescent coatings to primary and secondary structural steel members to achieve specified fire resistance ratings. Use factory-mixed single-pack thin-film coatings suitable for spray application. Verify steel members are properly prepared with compatible primer; primer must be fully cured and compatible with the intumescent system as certified by manufacturer. Surface preparation to meet relevant standards for cleanliness (typically EN ISO 8501-1) and profile (EN ISO 8503-2), with dust and contamination assessed visually or per EN ISO 8502-3. Provide enclosure as required to confine spraying, protect environment and maintain adequate ambient conditions (temperature, humidity, air quality, ventilation) during application. Protect intumescent coatings from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity and strong wind with dirt, dust or sand during application, drying and curing, unless evidence allows otherwise. Apply primer to DFT per manufacturer and EN ISO 12944-5; apply basecoat intumescent to DFT required for fire rating derived from EN 13381-4 test data and associated assessments; apply top sealer coat to DFT per manufacturer and EN ISO 12944-5. Do not apply subsequent coats until previous layers have fully cured. Provide uniform finish matching approved mockups. Measure wet and dry film thickness at each stage according to defined survey methodology and acceptance criteria, ensuring average DFT per element is at least nominal and localized readings not less than 50% of nominal, with strict rules for additional readings and remedial application in under-thickness areas.

Finish on external steel structures must satisfy a 'bright, light surface' requirement for relative absorptivity in accordance with NBN EN 1991-1-5 to control solar heat gain; coating colour and gloss to be selected to meet this requirement while compatible with corrosion and fire protection systems.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Fabrication and Execution Class
tolerances_and_rules: Fabricate structural steel members in accordance with all relevant EN codes including national annexes and complementary standards plus national best practice documents for steel buildings and bridges.
Shop fabricate to the greatest extent possible and fabricate for delivery sequence that expedites erection and minimizes field handling.
Identify and record materials and components with marks located for visibility after erection but not on exposed faces, subject to architect’s approval.
Complete assembly including welding of units before starting finishing operations where finishing is required, and provide exposed surfaces free of markings, burrs and defects.
Weld or bolt shop connections as indicated; bolt field connections except where welded or other connections are indicated.
Provide high-strength threaded fasteners for principal bolted connections and unfinished threaded fasteners only for secondary framing members and temporary bracing.
Install high-strength bolted assemblies in accordance with NBN EN 14399 and NBN EN 15048, with hardened washers under the turned element to facilitate verification inspection.
Carry out welded construction in accordance with NBN EN 1090 including all inspection, testing and acceptance requirements.
Assemble and weld built-up sections using methods that produce true alignment of axes without warp.
Prepare surfaces for shear connectors per manufacturer’s recommendations and perform automatic end welding of headed studs per manufacturer’s printed instructions.

Provide all necessary holes in structural members for fixing other work and for service penetrations as shown on final approved shop drawings, cutting, drilling or punching holes perpendicular to metal surfaces; do not flame cut holes or enlarge by burning; drill holes in bearing plates and remove burrs.
Develop required camber for members as indicated; where no camber is indicated fabricate beams so that any natural camber is upward after erection.
Steel used on the project to be designed and executed to Execution Class 2 (EXC2) under NBN EN 1090-2 unless noted otherwise on A/E drawings.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Connection Design and Detailing
tolerances_and_rules: Connections not detailed on drawings to be designed under direct supervision of a Professional Structural Engineer at Chartered/PE level experienced in structural steel.
Connections to be designed and detailed to resist loads and reactions shown in design documents and at least those required for robustness per NBN EN 1991, accounting for eccentricities.

Beam-to-column connections to minimize eccentric loading on columns; unrestrained simple beam end connections to be detailed and fabricated to minimize or eliminate end restraint of beams; welds, bolts and connection material to be designed for any eccentricity.

Beams to be designed for end shear reactions shown in design documents; bracing connections to be designed for specified forces; all member connections to be designed for relevant actions in project documents.

Except for moment connections and bracing, provide high-strength bolted bearing-type connections designed assuming threads included in shear plane; moment connections and bracing to use slip-critical bolted connections installed with direct tension indicator washers or tension-control assemblies in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.
Members forming bracing systems or lattice girders to be positioned so that lines of action intersect at a point unless otherwise detailed or instructed.
All shop and erection drawing connection details to be prepared under supervision of Contractor’s Engineer in accordance with NBN EN 1993.
Contractor to design and provide any required stiffener plates, doubler plates, reinforcing plates and their connections needed to develop or transfer forces specified in the Contract Documents.

All forces shown on drawings to be assumed reversible unless noted otherwise and connections to be checked for both directions. Where no forces are shown, connections to be designed for most critical combinations of member forces and directions.

For high-restraint welds, use double bevels instead of single bevels where practicable; detail joints to allow for weld shrinkage; for plate joints in more than one plane, show welding sequence on drawings and start welding at most restrained parts, proceeding to least restrained.

Connection design calculations to be uniquely numbered in a logical and consistent system; once submitted, numbers not to be changed; resubmissions indicated by same number with 'R' suffix and changes clouded; project may impose alternate numbering via BIM Execution Plan.

Provide clear sketches with all pertinent dimensions (pitch, gauge, edge distance, unbraced lengths, Whitmore lengths, etc.) for each connection design; geometry must be accurate and to scale with enough sketches to document full range of conditions.
For repetitive connections, provide summary tables from spreadsheets or programs referencing a standard calculation showing basis of design.
Provide drawings keyed to each connection calculation indicating locations of specific connection types.

Calculations to be typed or prepared via spreadsheet or computer program, or by another method approved by Engineer of Record, and must show all inputs and results for each step with explanatory text and sketches.
Provide calculation checks for all forces shown on drawings; all NBN EN 1993 code requirements to be applied; no use of 'OK by inspection' is permitted.

Before erection, at least 20 working days in advance, Contractor to survey the location, alignment and elevation of anchor rods installed by others and notify Design Professionals of any discrepancies; erection not to commence until any required corrective measures are completed.
Prior to erection of superstructure, accurately confirm anchor bolt alignment, elevations, projections and sizes; report inaccuracies or defects without delay.
Erect structural steel in compliance with local best practice guidance and NBN EN 1090 requirements for erection tolerances and quality, noting tolerances are absolute and not additive.
Allow for erection loads and provide sufficient temporary bracing to maintain structure in a safe condition, plumb and in true alignment until permanent bracing is installed.

Set structural frames accurately to lines and elevations indicated; align and adjust members forming part of a complete frame prior to permanent fastening; clean all bearing and contact surfaces before assembly; perform necessary adjustments to compensate for elevation and alignment discrepancies.
Align, level, adjust and plumb individual members within EN 1090 tolerances; splices only at locations indicated and accepted on shop drawings or as subsequently agreed.
Do not enlarge holes in members by burning or use of drift pins; ream holes that must be enlarged to admit bolts.

Do not use gas cutting torches in the field for correcting fabrication errors in structural framing unless acceptable to Engineer of Record; finish gas-cut sections to a sheared appearance when permitted.
Do not field cut or alter structural members without prior approval of Engineer of Record.
Erection is based on design assumption of minimum unrestrained temperature T0 = 10 °C; steel erection must be planned and executed to ensure this temperature assumption is met.
After erection, prime welds, abrasions and surfaces not shop primed, except surfaces in contact with concrete.
Grout solidly between column base plates and bearing surfaces using non-shrink grout, finished smooth and splayed at 45 degrees.
Steel erection must meet requirements corresponding to Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as specified in fabrication section.
Level and plumb individual structural members within EN 1090 erection tolerances.
Install steel deck in accordance with manufacturer’s written recommendations, approved submittals and project specification requirements.
Position deck units on supporting steel with units resting tightly on top of supporting members and aligned to final position.
Provide minimum bearing of 50 mm on steel supporting members.
Provide minimum end laps of 50 mm for roof deck units.
Cut deck neatly with metal saws, drills or cutting torch; cuts to be neat and trim in appearance.
Notch deck around columns and similar fabrications as required.
Cut holes and openings in deck in the field only where indicated on structural drawings and approved submittals.

Provide metal closures 1.5–1.58 mm wide and over to close panel edges and ends, column openings, and around penetrations; provide ridge and valley plates to ensure a surface acceptable to roofing contractor.

No openings may be cut in metal decking unless shown on approved submittals or specifically approved in writing by Engineer of Record. For unplanned openings, submit modified shop drawings and calculations for approval demonstrating compliance with all criteria.
Burning or weakening of metal deck around welds is cause for rejection; deficient welds must be repaired or removed and replaced.

Composite deck anchorage: provide 20 mm diameter puddle welds at each end and at intermediate supports of deck units with maximum effective average spacing of 300 mm across width; puddle welds not required where headed shear studs are welded through deck.
Composite deck long edges and side laps over steel members to be fastened with 20 mm puddle welds at maximum 300 mm spacing along length.
Composite deck longitudinal side laps not directly supported to be welded or fastened with minimum size self-tapping screws between supports with maximum spacing of 150 mm.

Composite deck longitudinal edge closures to be tack welded at maximum 600 mm spacing; sheet metal screws not permitted; closures and accessories to be adequately connected to framing steel and adjacent deck units.
Non-composite deck anchorage: provide 20 mm diameter puddle welds at each end and intermediate supports with maximum effective average spacing of 200 mm across width.
Non-composite deck long edges and side laps over steel members to be fastened with 20 mm puddle welds at maximum 300 mm spacing along length.
Non-composite deck longitudinal side laps without steel support to be welded or screwed with minimum size self-tapping screws between supports at maximum 150 mm spacing.

Non-composite deck longitudinal edge closures to be tack welded at maximum 150 mm spacing; sheet metal screws not permitted; closures and accessories to be adequately connected to framing steel and adjacent deck units.
Alternative mechanical anchoring systems such as proprietary fasteners (e.g., Hilti) may be used based on submitted and approved diaphragm design calculations.

Welding of shear studs through deck to primary steel members must ensure top beam surfaces are clean of mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint or other contaminants before laying deck, and welding must not be undertaken when ambient temperature is below 0 °C.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Fabrications – General Fabrication and Tolerances
tolerances_and_rules: Form metal fabrications from materials of sizes, thicknesses and shapes indicated but not less than required to satisfy performance requirements.
Fabricate to dimensions indicated or accepted on shop drawings using proven fabrication and support details.
Form exposed work true to line and level with accurate angles and straight sharp edges; shear and punch metals cleanly and accurately and remove burrs.
Ease exposed edges to approximately 1 mm radius unless otherwise indicated; form bent-metal corners to smallest radius possible without grain separation or impairment.
Remove sharp or rough areas on exposed traffic surfaces.
Weld corners and seams continuously to comply with EN 1011 recommendations and form exposed connections with hairline joints, flush and smooth, using concealed fasteners wherever possible.
Use exposed fasteners as indicated or Phillips flat-head countersunk screws/bolts where not indicated; locate joints to be least conspicuous.
Provide anchorage devices as indicated and coordinate with supporting structure; fabricate and space anchoring devices to provide adequate support for intended use.
Clearly mark shop-assembled and disassembled units for reassembly and coordinated installation.
Cut, reinforce, drill and tap miscellaneous metal work as required to receive hardware, screws and similar items.
Fabricate joints exposed to weather to exclude water or provide weep holes where water may accumulate.
Design fabrications for galvanizing to avoid distortion, including appropriate vent hole design and consideration of single-dip galvanizing for large articles or structural splicing where necessary.

Minimize internal stresses by preferring hot rolled sections over cold formed where possible, avoiding excessive jigs, minimizing weld size and amount, and using balanced welding sequences with uniform section thickness.

Fabrication tolerances include maximum 3 mm difference in diagonal measurements for squareness, maximum 2 mm offset between faces, maximum 2 mm misalignment between adjacent members, maximum bow of 3 mm in 1200 mm and maximum deviation from plane of 2 mm in 1200 mm.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Stairs and Ramps – Design and Installation
tolerances_and_rules: Clear widths, riser dimensions, going (tread depth) and pitch angles to meet local building code requirements.

Stair assemblies including landings and stringers to support a uniform live load of 500 kg/m² and a concentrated load of 150 kg applied over 2580 mm², with stringer and landing deflections not exceeding 1/360 of span.

Handrails and guardrails to be designed to withstand a uniform load of 1.0 kN/m applied at top rail in any direction and a concentrated 0.5 kN load applied at any point, without concurrent application of these loads. Infill areas to withstand horizontal uniform load of 1.0 kN/m² and point load 0.5 kN, not acting concurrent with top rail loads for guard stress checks.
At exit stairwells, provide self-supporting unit stair towers designed for stacking to full building height.
Provide stairs and railings meeting the most stringent requirements of European and applicable local regulations or project Contract Documents, whichever is more demanding.

Fabricate metal stair assemblies with commercial finish quality: exposed joints as inconspicuous as possible; underside of stair without soffit considered exposed to view; welded joints intermittently welded on back, filled with body putty and sanded smooth and flush; exposed welds ground smooth and flush; mechanical joints butted tight, flush and hairline; exposed bolts countersunk with flat or oval heads and no exposed nuts; exposed edges and corners eased to small uniform radius; surfaces to be painted or galvanized sanded or ground smooth for satin or matte finish.
Install stair components plumb and level, accurately fitted and free from distortion, providing temporary bracing to resist erection loads until permanent attachments are completed.
Provide anchors, plates, angles, hangers and struts for connecting stairs and ramps to building structure.

Where site welding is indicated, perform in accordance with EN 1011; for joints not specifically designated as welded, either welded or bolted joints are acceptable provided joint quality criteria are met.
Obtain approval before site cutting or making unscheduled adjustments; after erection, prime welds, abrasions and any unprimed or ungalvanized surfaces except surfaces in contact with concrete.
Tolerances for stair installation include maximum variation from plumb of 6 mm and maximum offset from true alignment of 6 mm for installed elements.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Handrails, Guards and Fixed Ladders – Installation
tolerances_and_rules: Fabricate pipe handrails and railing systems to comply with design, dimensions, detail and finish requirements and member sizes including wall thickness of pipe, post spacings and anchorage sufficient for structural loads.

Interconnect handrail and guard members by butt welding or by welding with internal connectors unless otherwise indicated; at tee and cross intersections, mitre intersecting members to match the contour of receiving pipe and weld fully around.

Form directional changes in handrails by welding prefabricated flush elbows, by radius bends of indicated radius or by flush radius bends or other specified methods; form simple and compound curves using bending jigs to maintain cylindrical cross section without buckling, twisting or cracking.
Provide wall returns at ends of wall-mounted handrails unless otherwise indicated; extend handrails beyond first and last nosing lines to comply with local code.
Close exposed pipe ends by welding 2 mm thick steel plates or using prefabricated fittings; locate drain or vent holes in inconspicuous positions and plug before delivery.

Provide wall brackets, end closures, flanges and miscellaneous fittings and anchors for pipe interconnections and attachment of handrails and guard systems to building structure; furnish inserts and anchorage for fixings to concrete or masonry.

Adjust handrails and guard systems before anchoring to ensure matching alignment at abutting joints; space posts at indicated points or as required by design loadings, ensuring posts are plumb in each direction.

Anchor posts to steel by direct welding to steel supporting members; anchor handrail ends to concrete or masonry with steel round flanges welded to rail ends and fixed with drilled-in expansion anchors.

Secure handrails to walls using brackets and end fittings providing at least 50 mm clearance from inside face of handrail to finished wall surface; install brackets at spacings required to support structural loads.

Use wall brackets with flanges tapped for concealed anchorage to threaded hanger bolts; for concrete or solid masonry, use drilled-in expansion anchors; for steel-framed gypsum board assemblies, fasten brackets to steel framing or concealed anchors with appropriate self-tapping screws.

Fixed ladders to include top and bottom supports and intermediate supports at no more than 1500 mm spacing, using welded or bolted steel brackets designed for adequate support and 175 mm minimum clearance from wall to rung centreline; ladder rails to extend at least 1100 mm above top rung and return to wall or structure with goose-neck arrangements if required.

Fixed ladder rungs to be spaced 225–300 mm vertically with consistent spacing in each flight and maximum 6 m height between landings; rungs to be at least 175 mm clear from wall surface and fitted into side rails, plug welded and ground smooth on outer faces.
Provide safety cage hoops as required above 3 m from finished floor level or as indicated, and guardrails 1100 mm high at fixed ladder landings to EN 14122.
All external railings, stairs and ramps including associated components to be factory pre-finished for C4 environment class per EN ISO 12944-2 and ISO 9223.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Pre-Construction and Pre-Erection Coordination for Structural Steel
tolerances_and_rules: At least 14 days before beginning structural steel erection, Contractor must hold a pre-construction conference to review detailed quality control and construction requirements and plan procedures for achieving required steel construction quality, including submittal requirements, coordination status, material availability, work progress schedule, and procedures for inspection, testing, certifications and reporting.

Attendance at structural steel pre-construction conference to include responsible representatives from Construction Manager, Contractor’s Site Engineer, Special Inspection and Testing Agency, Structural Steel detailer, fabricator, erector, Engineer of Record and Architect if required.
Contractor to record, type and distribute meeting minutes within 5 days, sending copies at least to Owner’s Representative, Architect and Engineer of Record.

Contractor to notify all external parties at least 7 days in advance of scheduled conference date and bears full responsibility for organizing the meeting within the required timeframe; failure is considered indicative of poor attention to specified requirements and quality procedures.

Pre-construction conference and associated documentation do not replace formal submittals and approvals; comments made by A/E of Record at the meeting are not binding and do not preclude them from expressing different views during formal reviews or site inspections.
At least 20 working days before commencing steel erection, Contractor must hold a structural steel pre-erection conference to review detailed erection requirements.

Pre-erection conference attendees must include, at minimum, General Contractor/Construction Manager, Steel Erector/Fabricator, Erector’s Surveyor, Roof Deck Contractor, all testing and inspection agencies, design professionals, Owner, and Precast or Cladding Contractor as appropriate.

Contractor to prepare agenda and record and distribute minutes within 5 working days to all participants. Minutes must include detailed erection procedure outline plus schedule of milestone dates for surveys and sign-offs on erection stages agreed by all parties, and the surveying program and submission schedule for approvals.
Structural Engineer of Record is explicitly not responsible for, and has no charge over, safety programs or site safety precautions notwithstanding any other provision.

Responsibility for organizing pre-erection conference and compliance with all associated requirements lies exclusively with Contractor; conferences are not to be used to seek approvals and failure to comply indicates poor attention to specified procedures.

At least 20 working days before starting connection design and detailing, Fabricator must hold a workshop to verify all connection design assumptions and procedures as well as shop drawing preparation and submittal procedures.
Workshop attendees to include, at minimum, representatives of General Contractor, Fabricator, Detailer, Connection Engineer, Engineer of Record and Erector.
Fabricator to prepare an agenda prior to the workshop and distribute detailed meeting minutes within 5 working days.

Responsibility to organize the workshop within required timeframe and meet all related requirements rests entirely with Contractor; failure indicates poor attention to specified requirements and quality processes.
Connection design and detailing workshop is not a substitute for formal submittals and approvals; it cannot be used to obtain approvals and comments from A/E of Record at workshop are not binding.
Any subsequent A/E comments during formal review of documentation, samples or site work may differ from workshop discussions without prejudice.

qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide shop drawings for individual structural steel shipping pieces prior to fabrication, prepared and checked by a suitably qualified professional Structural Engineer. Include member sizes, lengths, orientations, holes, camber, connection details and all required information for fabrication and erection. Provide separate erection drawings and method statements showing field installation and member placement, indicating locations and connection details of each shipping piece.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Temporary Works and Erection Method Statements – Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit temporary works drawings and method statements prepared by the steel erector, illustrating sequence of erection, requirements for temporary supports, and requirements for lifting, bolting and welding. Information must include sequence of work, bracing locations, temporary supports and descriptions of bolting, welding of connections and lifting operations. These documents must be submitted and accepted before erection and coordinated with pre-erection conference outcomes.

Submit complete design calculations for all designed connections before preparation of shop drawings. Calculations must be performed and sealed by a Professional Structural Engineer and must comply with NBN EN 1993 and project loads. Number each calculation in a logical system and maintain numbers for resubmissions (adding 'R' suffix and clouding changes). Include sketches with accurate geometry, key dimensions, Whitmore length assumptions and diagrams. Provide summary tables for repetitive connections and keyed location drawings. All checks must be calculated explicitly; 'OK by inspection' is not permitted.

Submit a Quality Plan for execution of structural steel works in accordance with recommendations of NBN EN 1090 as early as possible after appointment. The plan must describe fabrication, welding, bolting, inspection, testing, documentation, and traceability procedures aligned with the specified Execution Class 2 (EXC2) and must be followed throughout the work.

Provide manufacturer’s mill certificates for all structural steel products, certifying compliance with specified grades and standards (e.g., NBN EN 10025 S355JR, NBN EN 10210 S355JR, NBN EN 10346 S350). Submit certificates for welding electrodes verifying conformity with specified standards. Provide documentation for shear studs, direct tension indicators, grout and other accessories as required.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Welder Certifications – Structural Steel and Decking
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit certificates for all welders employed on structural steel and steel deck work, demonstrating qualification in accordance with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 within the previous 12 months. Maintain qualification records for deck welders and ensure they are tested per standard qualification procedures of relevant welding standards. For stud welding on deck, ensure welders are certified by an authority recognized in the project location.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Contractor and Fabricator Qualifications – Structural Steel and Fabrications
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Confirm membership of the structural steel fabricator in the national Constructional Steelwork Association or other relevant organization. Provide confirmation of CE Marking accreditation for the Execution Class relevant to the project (EXC2). Demonstrate that the fabricator has experience producing similar metal fabrications and that they have sufficient production capacity. For stairs and ramps, demonstrate fabricator experience with similar stair systems and provide structural designer qualifications as Professional Engineer licensed locally.

Contractor must declare and verify in writing in structural steel submittals that steel contains 70% recycled content (pre-consumer and post-consumer). Copies of this declaration must be sent concurrently to EXE and DC Sustainability for tracking. If compliance cannot be achieved due to availability, schedule or cost impacts, Contractor must submit a written request for exception to the Engineer of Record at time of submittal with copies to EXE and DC Sustainability.

For both structural steel pre-construction and pre-erection conferences, Contractor must prepare agendas, conduct meetings within specified timelines (14 days before erection for pre-construction; 20 working days before erection for pre-erection), record and type minutes within 5 days, and distribute to all involved parties including Owner’s Representative, Architect and Engineer of Record. Contractor must notify external parties at least 7 days prior to each conference and ensure minutes document agreed erection procedures, survey programs and milestone sign-off schedules.

Submit shop drawings for steel decking showing deck profile, type, identification marks, gauge, finish, locations, openings, dimensions, placement sequence, anchorage details, lap details, accessories, welding data, power requirements and electrode types. Indicate welding symbols per relevant European welding standards. Show unframed openings including those cut after concrete placement, deck closure details, reinforcement details and type and location of inserts.

Provide product data for deck systems including profile characteristics, dimensions, section properties, material grade (e.g., S350 per NBN EN 10346/10143), and finishes. Data must demonstrate compliance with design and performance requirements and relevant standards including NBN EN 1993 Part 1-3 and NBN EN 1090.

Submit design calculations for steel deck prepared and sealed by a Professional Engineer specializing in structural engineering. Calculations must include section properties for each deck type and gauge, and design of slab edge and closure strips. Shop drawings will not be reviewed without these calculations; approval does not relieve engineer of design responsibility.

Maintain welder qualification data for deck welding available for examination. Qualify welders by tests in accordance with standard qualification procedures of relevant welding standards. Where stricter standards or regulations do not apply, each welder must prepare two specimens of each weld type required, to be inspected, tested and approved by the Inspection and Testing Agency prior to welding on structure.

Submit shop drawings for all metal fabrications indicating profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, size and type of fasteners and accessories. Include erection drawings, elevations and detail views where applicable. Depict all welded connections using standard ISO 2553 symbols and indicate net weld lengths.
Submit certification for welders employed on metal fabrications verifying suitable qualification within the previous 12 months and in compliance with EN 1011 and relevant local welding codes.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Shop Drawings – Metal Stairs and Ramps
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide shop drawings for metal stairs, ramps, handrails and guards showing profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, fastener types and sizes, treads, risers, stringers, landings, guard infills, rail details and finishes. Indicate welded connections using standard welding symbols and net weld lengths. Include design engineer’s signature on each sheet attesting to code compliance and design loads.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Fabricator and Structural Designer Qualifications – Stairs and Ramps
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Demonstrate that stair fabricator has experience producing similar steel stairs with successful in-service performance. Provide documentation of structural designer qualifications as a Professional Engineer experienced in stair design and licensed in the jurisdiction of the project.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Fireproofing – Product Data and Test Evidence
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit product data sheets for each intumescent fire protection system including primers, basecoat and top sealer. For each system, provide test results from an independent fire test laboratory based on EN 13381-4 and an assessment of results used to calculate required coating thickness for the full range of section sizes. Assessments must be issued through an organization subscribing to the Passive Fire Protection Federation 'Guide to Undertaking Assessments in Lieu of Fire Tests.' Provide product certificates confirming compatibility of intumescent coatings with primers, adhesives and surface coatings on steel substrates. Submit tabulated or printed DFT requirements versus steel section factor for each product type to demonstrate compliance with specified fire rating series on project drawings.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Fireproofing – Installer Qualifications and References
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide qualification data showing that the intumescent coatings installer is certified, licensed or otherwise approved by the coatings manufacturer, with staff trained by manufacturer’s direct employees. Submit evidence of previous comparable projects including project locations, scope of work, contract values, completion dates and contact information for architects and owners. Confirm manufacturer’s local technical representation and commitment to attend site at start of installation and as required.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Field Quality Control – Structural Steel and Bolting
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: An independent testing agency engaged under Section 01 40 00 must perform field quality control tests for structural steel. Testing must include verification of high-strength field-bolted connections and visual inspection of all field-welded connections. Failed tests must be followed by re-inspection at no additional cost or time to Owner. Contractor is solely responsible for any corrective measures resulting from detailing, fabrication and erection errors.

An independent testing agency must perform site quality control for steel deck installation. All field-welded connections, including puddle welds and shear stud welds, must be visually inspected for adequacy and conformance to specified sizes and spacings. Any deficiencies must be repaired or replaced and may require additional inspection by the independent agency.

An independent testing agency appointed under Section 01 40 00 must carry out field quality control inspections for intumescent coatings. Scope includes verification of surface preparation standards (EN ISO 8501-1) and surface profile (EN ISO 8503-2), checks for dust and contamination (visual or EN ISO 8502-3), and monitoring air and substrate temperatures, relative humidity and dew point during application to confirm compliance with specification or manufacturer’s data sheet. Agency must record batch numbers, dates and times of application and adherence to over-coating intervals, perform wet film thickness checks and dry film thickness surveys at primer, intumescent basecoat and completed coating stages. Acceptance criteria require average DFT per element at or above nominal, average DFT on any face at least 80% of nominal, with limited isolated readings under 80% subject to additional local measurements and remedial applications; no readings may be less than 50% of nominal, and average DFT must not exceed manufacturer’s recommended maximum for any member shape and orientation.
